name: Fairlight CMI Series I
known_for: Described by Museums Victoria as the first commercially available digital sampling instrument.

name: E-mu Emulator
known_for: E-mu's first sampler; about 500 were sold before it was discontinued in early 1984.

name: E-mu Emulator II
known_for: The 1984 successor to the Emulator.

name: Ensoniq Mirage
time: about 3 seconds, as Hank Shocklee recalled
known_for: Brought sampling down to $1,695 when an Emulator cost about $8,000.

name: Fairlight CMI Series III
known_for: Took the Fairlight to 16-bit stereo and 16 voices.

name: E-mu SP-12
known_for: Dave Rossum's sampling drum machine and the predecessor of the SP-1200.

name: Casio SK-1
known_for: A toy-priced sampling keyboard with a built-in microphone that became a circuit-bending standard.

name: Akai S900
time: 750 KB; 63 seconds at 7.5 kHz, a little under 12 seconds at top quality
known_for: An eight-voice 12-bit sampler that let the user trade sample rate for time.

name: E-mu SP-1200
known_for: The gritty 12-bit drum sampler credited with the crunchy drums and filtered basslines of late-1980s and 1990s hip-hop.

name: Akai S950
time: 750 KB, expandable to 2,250 KB; 9.89 seconds at 48 kHz
known_for: Its time-stretch, from 1% to 999%, became part of the sound of 1990s jungle.

name: Akai S1000
known_for: Moved the Akai S-series to 16-bit stereo.

name: Akai MPC60
known_for: Sixteen pads, a 99-track sequencer and Roger Linn's swing.

name: Ensoniq ASR-10
known_for: Used by RZA, Kanye West, Timbaland, The Neptunes, Prince Paul and The Alchemist.

name: Akai MPC3000
known_for: Added 32 voices, a filter and effects; J Dilla's Limited Edition unit is in the Smithsonian.

name: Akai MPC2000
known_for: The first MPC designed without Roger Linn.

name: Boss SP-202 Dr. Sample
known_for: The first of the SP line, with eight pads.

name: Boss SP-303 Dr. Sample
known_for: Its Vinyl Sim and tape echo are credited on Madvillainy and Donuts.

name: Roland SP-404
known_for: Twelve pads, 29 effects and a CompactFlash slot; the sampler of the beat scene around Flying Lotus, Ras G and Dibia$e.

name: Akai MPC One
known_for: A standalone MPC with a 7-inch touchscreen and no battery.

name: Native Instruments Maschine+
known_for: The first Maschine that runs without a computer.

name: Roland SP-404MKII
known_for: The current SP-404, with an OLED screen and Skip Back Sampling.

name: Teenage Engineering EP-133 K.O. II
time: 64 MB at launch; 128 MB standard from January 2026
known_for: A 12-pad sampler with 999 sample slots at a $299 launch price.
